conflicts.issue: Confederate Monument Base Relocation Options (Beechwood Cemetery) and 2015 State Statute Compliance
conflicts.summary: During review of the City-County Committee on Confederate Monuments report, members and presenters clashed over two elements of the committee's unanimous recommendations: listing Beechwood Cemetery (a historic African American cemetery) alongside Maplewood Cemetery as a conditional future relocation site for the Confederate monument base if state law changes, and whether adding new pillars to the existing base is legally permissible under North Carolina's 2015 monument protection statute.
conflicts.side_a_position: Committee report included both city-owned cemeteries as conditional options if state law changes and proposed contextualizing the base with Union and enslaved-people pillars.
side_a_arguments: All 12 committee members reached consensus on listing Maplewood or Beechwood cemeteries only as conditional future options if North Carolina's 2015 monument law changes.
Legal speakers presented conflicting views on whether the 2015 statute governs a monument that was pulled down and catastrophically damaged.
Co-chairs acknowledged in hindsight that perhaps both city-owned cemeteries should not have been included given the historical relationship with Beechwood.
conflicts.side_b_position: Objected strongly to naming Beechwood Cemetery for any Confederate monument base relocation and urged legal review of altering the existing base under state law.
side_b_arguments: There are no Confederate dead buried at Beechwood Cemetery, a historic African American cemetery, making the suggestion deeply inappropriate and hurtful.
The 2015 state monument statute appears to prohibit altering the existing monument base, warranting formal review by City and County Attorneys.
conflicts.resolution: Committee unanimously passed a motion referring the report to the City and County Managers and City and County Attorneys for legal and policy guidance, while explicitly noting that Beechwood Cemetery should not be included for relocating the Confederate base.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee
meetings.executive_summary: The Joint City-County Committee met on October 8, 2019, approving the August 13 minutes (with a later agreed clarification noting that City and County staff would collaborate on the joint tax relief strategy ahead of budget decisions), the draft 2020 meeting schedule, and a reappointment item by uncontested voice votes. DataWorks NC presented interactive visualizations on Durham's eviction crisis (citing roughly 2,488 annual evictions and ~25.7 daily filings), prompting committee questions on seasonality, voucher landlord opt-outs, and state tenant-law reform. Staff then led an extended briefing on unsheltered homelessness and street outreach after Alliance Behavioral Healthcare cut its 10-year street outreach funding due to state budget reductions. While the City proposed reprioritizing existing homelessness system-building funds and noted $122,000 in spring 2020 center and security savings, the County was asked to prepare an interlocal agreement and mid-year funding contribution once $77,000 in carryover funding expires.

agenda_items.title: Approval of August 13, 2019 Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The committee approved the August 13, 2019 meeting minutes by voice vote, seconded by Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson. After Item 2, a member returned to the minutes at 00:02:58 to request adding a sentence clarifying that City and County staff agreed to work together on the Joint City-County tax relief strategy and return with options in time for budget decisions. The chair agreed to insert that clarification without objection.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Draft 2020 Joint City-County Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members reviewed the draft 2020 Joint City-County meeting calendar included in the agenda packet. Following brief discussion about potentially skipping the January 2020 meeting after a December 2019 session, members agreed to leave it to the Mayor and the BOCC Chair to decide based on agenda volume. The schedule was approved by voice vote, seconded by Jillian Johnson.

agenda_items.title: Reappointment Item (Tax Relief / Committee Appointment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The committee considered a reappointment item referenced in the automated captions as a reappointment connected to city tax relief (the appointee's name was garbled in the transcript ASR). A motion and second were made from the floor, and the item passed by voice vote without objection.

agenda_items.title: Eviction Data Project Presentation (DataWorks NC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A health data analyst from DataWorks NC presented interactive online visualizations examining Durham's eviction crisis, including roughly 2,488 annual evictions (about 6.81 evictions and 25.7 filings per day, or roughly 200 evictions per month). Members asked about seasonal spikes after December, winter heating costs, landlords declining Housing Choice Vouchers, comparisons to New York, and grassroots efforts to reform state landlord-tenant laws. A member requested follow-up confirmation on the monthly eviction figures.

agenda_items.title: Unsheltered Homelessness, Street Outreach Funding & Encampment Response
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City and County staff briefed the committee on unsheltered homelessness and street outreach after Alliance Behavioral Healthcare abruptly ended 10 years of street outreach funding due to state-driven budget cuts, leaving Housing for New Hope operating temporarily on roughly $77,000 in carryover funds. Staff outlined best practices—consistent trust-building outreach, harm reduction, housing-first, street coordinated entry, team case management, a pilot RFP, and coordinated encampment response—alongside a conceptual reinvestment of $122,000/year in center operations ($72,000) and security ($50,000) ending in spring 2020. Commissioners raised concerns about late notification from Alliance (noting Heidi Carter as the County's Alliance representative), ER utilization, permanent supportive housing needs alongside the housing bond, and coordination with EMS and jail discharges, while staff outlined an interlocal agreement and mid-year County budget request for spring 2020.

votes.notes: Voice vote; individual member roll call and attendance list were not read into the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved from the floor (mover name garbled in ASR as 'now') and seconded by Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson. At 00:03:00–00:04:39, the committee agreed without objection to insert a clarifying sentence noting City and County staff would collaborate on the Joint City-County tax relief strategy and report back ahead of budget decisions.

votes.notes: Voice vote; mover name not captured clearly in ASR and individual votes were not polled.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the draft 2020 meeting calendar with consensus that the Mayor and BOCC Chair may cancel the January 2020 meeting if agenda items are insufficient.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Steve Schewel on May 14, 2019, the Joint City-County Committee approved its March 12 meeting minutes by unanimous voice vote and followed up on Durham's HIV rate resolution, which Public Health staff confirmed had been supported by the Board of Health and would return during County budget sessions. Staff from the Office on Youth presented an update on the City-County Strategic Youth Initiative, detailing three goals focused on equitable youth decision-making, stakeholder engagement via a Youth Listening Project and Kumu service mapping, and internal capacity building. Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, the committee concluded a discussion on tenant eviction right-to-counsel models in New York and Philadelphia for upcoming budget consideration, heard a report from PEACH on primary prevention of childhood lead poisoning and pre-1978 housing code violations, and heard Mayor Schewel place a potential joint citywide expansion of the long-term low-income homeowner tax relief program on the County's radar before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Approval of March 12, 2019 Minutes and HIV Rate Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The committee approved the March 12, 2019 minutes by voice vote with no opposition. Afterward, a member asked whether the partnership's presentation on Durham's HIV rate had gone before the Board of Health in April as noted in the minutes. Public Health staff confirmed the presentation took place, the Board of Health supported the resolution, staffing funding would be discussed during upcoming County budget sessions, and Durham's updated ranking was fourth or fifth in North Carolina.

agenda_items.title: City-County Strategic Youth Initiative and Office on Youth Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Office on Youth staff updated the committee on absorbing the Youth Initiatives Manager role into three strategic priorities: equitable youth engagement without tokenism, strengthening the impact of City- and County-supported youth services, and building internal organizational capacity. Presenters described parallel adult training to address adultism, youth racial equity training, connecting local youth groups with the Durham Youth Commission (DYC), the Youth Listening Project, and building a service inventory in Kumu.

agenda_items.title: Eviction Representation and Tenant Right-to-Counsel Discussion (Conclusion)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle section truncated in the transcript digest, the concluding exchange covered phased tenant attorney funding and right-to-counsel models in New York and Philadelphia. A committee member noted upcoming budget sessions to place the item on the agenda, and the presenter agreed to email the PowerPoint, handout, and New York and Philadelphia studies.

agenda_items.title: PEACH Report on Childhood Lead Poisoning Primary Prevention
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Invited by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, the director of the Partnership Effort for the Advancement of Children's Health (PEACH) presented three years of grassroots work advocating a transition to primary prevention of childhood lead poisoning. The report cited CDC guidance, a 2007 Duke study linking blood lead levels of 2–5 micrograms per deciliter to 14–15% drops in math and reading scores, under-50% screening rates in Durham, and over 1,600 Neighborhood Improvement Services code violations for deteriorated paint in pre-1978 housing. Recommendations spanned education and outreach, pediatric testing, contractor lead-safe enforcement, a policy packet for the Board of Health, and potential state statutory review for joint City-County inspections.

agenda_items.title: Other Business: Potential Citywide Low-Income Homeowner Tax Relief Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before adjourning, Mayor Steve Schewel notified County Commissioners that the City Council and Community Development staff were exploring expanding the City's long-term, low-income homeowner tax relief program—currently limited to three neighborhoods—citywide. He emphasized that pursuing such a program would require County participation and formally placed the long-term concept on the joint agenda for future discussion.

votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual attendance were not named in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion and second made from the floor; approved by voice vote with 'Aye' and no opposition ('Opposed? No.').

meetings.title: Joint City-County Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel presided over the January 8, 2019 Joint City-County Meeting, where the committee unanimously approved the November 13, 2018 minutes, the 2019 meeting calendar, and Durham's AARP Age-Friendly Community letter and application on motions by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton. Staff presented a draft interlocal agreement for conveying County tax-foreclosed parcels to the City for affordable housing (with 7 of ~25 reviewed lots appearing buildable) and Downtown Durham Inc. presented findings from its East Main Street planning charrette. The 12-member City-County Committee on Confederate Monuments then presented unanimous recommendations to preserve the toppled Confederate statue in its damaged state, retain and add Union soldier and enslaved-people pillars to the courthouse base, and conditionally relocate the base to Maplewood or Beechwood cemeteries if state law changes. After contentious debate over legal constraints under the 2015 state monument statute and strong objections to naming historic African American Beechwood Cemetery as a relocation site, the committee voted unanimously to thank the committee and refer the report to the City and County Managers and Attorneys while noting Beechwood should be excluded.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 13, 2018 Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The committee took up the circulated minutes of the November 13, 2018 Joint City-County meeting. On a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, the minutes passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Approval of 2019 Joint City-County Meeting Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Steve Schewel acknowledged Commissioner Wendy Jacobs for her work preparing the 2019 calendar, noting it skips the July meeting as usual. Moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, the calendar passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: AARP Age-Friendly Community Letter and Application
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Gail Harris presented the letter and application for Durham to join the AARP Age-Friendly Community network and complete an aging plan within a year. Mayor Steve Schewel and another member thanked the County for leading the effort alongside City Parks and Recreation and transportation roles. Moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Brenda A. Howerton, the motion to approve and sign the letter and application passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Interlocal Agreement for Conveyance of Tax-Foreclosed Parcels for Affordable Housing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff briefed the committee on implementing the County's November 2018 policy to convey tax-foreclosed lots to the City for affordable housing prior to public bidding, noting a draft interlocal agreement memorializing 3- and 5-year deed terms and an 80% AMI maximum (with City staff evaluating 30–60% AMI targets per project) was expected before City Council in February. Out of roughly 25 parcels reviewed, 7 appeared buildable, 12 remained under review, and 6 were constrained. Members questioned whether adjacent lots could be combined/rezoned and whether 'buildable lots only' should specify a percentage threshold outside floodplains and stream buffers.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI) Presentation on East Main Street Charrette
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel introduced the DDI presentation on the East Main Street charrette (noting he and Ellen W. Reckhow attended, and announcing Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson would arrive late due to another committee meeting). The presenter summarized breakout-team recommendations covering big-picture urban design issues, greenway connections along the railroad tracks, and street tree enhancements along East Main Street before the digest's middle truncation.

agenda_items.title: City-County Committee on Confederate Monuments Report and Referral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Co-chairs of the 12-member City-County Committee on Confederate Monuments presented unanimous recommendations to preserve the toppled Confederate statue as an artifact with multi-university interpretive text, add new pillars honoring Union soldiers and enslaved people around the existing courthouse base, and conditionally relocate the base to Maplewood or Beechwood cemeteries if North Carolina's 2015 monument law is changed. Debate centered on conflicting legal interpretations of whether altering the base violates the 2015 statute and sharp objections from a committee official against naming Beechwood—a historic African American cemetery with no Confederate dead—as a relocation site. The committee unanimously approved a motion to thank the advisory committee and refer its report to the City and County Managers and Attorneys for review, noting Beechwood should not be included.

votes.notes: Voice vote declared unanimous by Chair Steve Schewel; full present member roll call was not recorded in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton; passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2019 Joint City-County Meeting Calendar
votes.notes: Voice vote declared unanimous by Chair Steve Schewel; full present member roll call was not recorded in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the 2019 calendar prepared with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs, continuing the practice of skipping the July meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of AARP Age-Friendly Community Letter and Application
votes.notes: Voice vote declared unanimous by Chair Steve Schewel; full present member roll call was not recorded in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton to approve and sign the AARP Age-Friendly Community letter and application as submitted.

votes.item_title: Thank Confederate Monuments Committee and Refer Report to Managers and Attorneys
votes.notes: Voice vote declared unanimous; mover and seconder names were not spoken in the transcript digest, and Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson had been noted earlier as arriving late.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to formally thank the 12-member Committee on Confederate Monuments for its work and refer its report to the City and County Managers and City and County Attorneys for review and guidance to both boards, with discussion noting for the record that Beechwood Cemetery should not be included as a relocation option.
